tooling_constraint: GitHub MCP is scoped to bolyra/bolyra. External PR state CANNOT be queried live. This is the same root cause that triggered the pause. External PR statuses below reflect last live verification on 2026-07-27. No state changes have been written to prs.json this cycle to avoid producing another false-data record.

pr_status_summary.action_needed: none — founder decision: leave all 9 open PRs alone. No bumps, no closes.

new_targets.why: Active A2A x402 protocol implementation with a confirmed settlement-gating race condition (issue #121, 7 comments, last activity 2026-07-28). Maintainers are engaged: issue #60 on spending limits has 9 comments over 5 months. This is the closest thing to a real bug Bolyra can fix rather than add as an example.
new_targets.gap: Agent delegate execution runs BEFORE payment settlement is confirmed (issue #121). No agent identity/credential layer — any caller can invoke a delegate action. Bolyra's @bolyra/mpp mandate check gate + bounded permission model (FINANCIAL_SMALL/MEDIUM bits) is the precise fix.
new_targets.pr_type: bug-fix — add a pre-execution mandate-check middleware that gates delegate invocation. Reference Bolyra EVC as the verifier interface (spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md). No Bolyra dependency required in the target repo.

new_targets.why: Trust layer for agent commerce with ERC-7710 delegated permissions and x402. Issue #3 explicitly asks for an off-chain reasoning-level verifier — Bolyra's External Verifier Contract (EVC) is exactly that interface. Maintainer is actively building (created 2026-06-16, updated today). High star count signals fast-growing project.
new_targets.gap: Issue #3: 'Layer 6 coverage gap: no off-chain reasoning-level verifier.' The repo has on-chain escrow + ERC-7710 delegation but no classical or ZK verifier for pre-action credential checks. Bolyra's EVC v1 (stdin/stdout JSON contract) is a drop-in.
new_targets.pr_type: bug-fix/feature — implement a bolyra-evc adapter plugin that satisfies issue #3. The EVC interface is already open-spec (spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md) so the PR can reference it without depending on Bolyra packages.

new_targets.why: AI agent that spends USDC autonomously via x402. No spending-cap enforcement at the authorization layer — any action can drain the wallet. Active repo (BlockRunAI also maintains ClawRouter 6683★). Low issue count means PRs get attention.
new_targets.gap: Franklin has no pre-spend limit check before executing tool calls that trigger x402 payments. Bolyra's FINANCIAL_SMALL (<$100) and FINANCIAL_MEDIUM (<$10K) permission bits map directly to a per-action budget guard. A targeted fix in the payment-dispatch path prevents runaway spend.
new_targets.pr_type: targeted fix — add a budget-guard middleware in Franklin's payment dispatch. Implement the check using the Bolyra permission-bit semantics without requiring a Bolyra dependency (the guard logic is simple enough to inline with a comment pointing to the spec).

new_targets.why: MCP server with pay-per-call x402 micropayments for live data tools. Updated today. No per-tool authorization check — any MCP client can call any tool, bypassing the payment gate if the x402 middleware is misconfigured. Same BlockRunAI team as Franklin/ClawRouter = high chance they'd accept a consistent authorization story across their stack.
new_targets.gap: x402 payment is checked at the HTTP layer but there is no agent-identity binding — a client can forge or replay a payment token for a different tool. Bolyra @bolyra/mpp's `bolyraGate()` adds mandate-verified dispatch; the fix is a thin wrapper on the MCP tool handler.
new_targets.pr_type: targeted fix — wrap the MCP tool dispatch with a mandate-check gate. Can reference the bolyra mandate issuance CLI as a companion without adding a runtime dependency.

new_targets.why: CLI for agentic payments (x402, MPP, AP2). Issue #371 is an open design proposal for a risk/collateral layer (5 comments, 2026-07-26 activity). Solana Foundation ownership means a merged PR here is very high-credibility. Rust implementation may limit easy integration, but the design proposal issue opens a documentation/spec PR path.
new_targets.gap: Issue #371: no risk/collateral layer for x402-paid agents — agents can initiate payments without identity-bound spending limits. Bolyra's mandate issuance model (operator-signed spend mandates with cumulative-bit permissions) is a concrete answer to the design proposal.
new_targets.pr_type: design/spec PR — add a AGENTS.md that maps Bolyra's mandate model to the `pay` CLI's x402 flow, responding to issue #371 with a concrete proposal. Not code, but a well-reasoned design doc is the correct PR type for a Rust CLI where a Bolyra integration would live upstream.
